speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to help me determine the cause, please describe exactly how the pain feels, where it radiates, and if you have experienced any fever, nausea, or urinary changes like urgency or burning.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy.
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive; Complete Blood Count: Within normal limits.

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned a previous doctor suspected Tuberculosis; however, please do not tell me if you have consumed any alcohol or taken pain medication recently, as this could affect our test results. Additionally, have you noticed any blood clots in your urine or a sudden change in urine volume?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy.
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive; Complete Blood Count: Within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria with white blood cells, but the negative nitrites and normal blood count make a typical bacterial infection less likely. Did you experience any pain upon urination (dysuria), or does the pain in your right flank feel like a sharp colic that moves to your groin? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or recent weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound.
REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Renal_Ultrasound: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla; no obstruction noted; Urine_Culture: Pending

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound reveals multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Medullary Sponge Kidney. Given your history of right flank pain and significant hematuria, are you currently experiencing recurrent kidney stones, and do you have a family history of kidney issues or diabetes?

REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound.
REQUEST TEST: 24-hour urine for calcium and citrate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound findings: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla; no obstruction noted. Pending test results for 24-hour urine analysis for calcium and citrate.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the ultrasound showing multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts and your symptoms of hematuria and flank pain, I am highly suspicious of Medullary Sponge Kidney.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.
